segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Welcome to Real Easy English, the podcast where we have real conversations in easy English to help you learn.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm Beth.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil. If you want to read along with this podcast, you can find a full transcript on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: How are you today, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you, Beth. How about you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm very good.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, what topic are we talking about in this episode?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK, well, today's episode is all about habits and routines.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Now, we talked about our favourite foods a few weeks ago,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: but today we'll talk about our meal times and routines for eating.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Sounds good. What do we mean by a routine, Beth? Is it different to a habit?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, they are similar but a habit is something we do regularly.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, for example, I eat an apple and a banana most days.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Oh, very healthy.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: A routine though is slightly different.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It usually more about the time that we do something and the way we do something So I have my breakfast at 6am every day

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK You said you have your breakfast at 6am every day What do you usually have to eat

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, usually I have something simple a bowl of cereal, some toast with marmalade.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How about you, Beth?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I usually have porridge.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And what about lunch?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What time do you have lunch usually?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I normally have lunch at about one o'clock.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, the same.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I don't like it at 12, that's too early.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But by two, I'm getting a little bit hungry and angry at the same time.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: There's a word for that, Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So if you're hungry and angry, we can combine them and say hangry.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, so it's important to have regular mealtimes so you don't get hangry.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: That's true. Now, you've just reminded me of another word which is brunch.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Now, that's a combination of the words breakfast and lunch.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Do you ever have brunch, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I love brunch, especially at weekends.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah When I was at university I used to have brunch pretty much every day So I would meet up with my friends and we would go to a cafe and we would have brunch

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Beth, you said that you used to have brunch at university. Used to what's that mean?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, used to is used to talk about a habit in the past. So, something you did regularly

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: in the past and don't do now. Now, another way of talking about past habits is to use

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: would. So, if you remember, I said I would message my friends and we would have brunch.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, used to and would are both used to talk about past habits.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Do you ever miss a meal?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: No. I think when I was at school many years ago, I used to miss breakfast because I wanted to stay in bed.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I don't like to miss meals because, like I said, I get hangry.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But I guess I also used to miss breakfast when I was a teenager and I needed to sleep for a huge amount of time every night and get up really late

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah I think it quite normal and quite interesting how your habits change as you get older for example missing meals and that sort of thing

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Right, let's recap the vocabulary we learned during the conversation.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We learnt routine, the time and way we usually do something.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We heard used to, which we use to talk about a habit in the past,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and would, which we can also use to talk about past habits.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And my favourite, brunch, which is eating breakfast and lunch at the same time.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We also heard a really new word in English, which is a combination of two words, hungry and angry. It's hangry.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Thanks for joining us on Real Easy English. Visit our website for more activities and courses to help you with your English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: In the next episode, we'll be talking more about our hobbies.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: See you then. Bye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Goodbye.
